idiom_name: generic wrapper struct implementing the same trait, or impl Fn composition
implementation_notes: Rust has no component type and no inheritance, so the enhancer is written explicitly: a generic wrapper struct that owns the wrapped component and implements the same trait, forwarding calls inside the trait impl, or a higher-order function over closures that returns impl Fn - the Fn trait documented in std::ops is the bound describing callable values. Box<dyn Component> makes the wrapper dynamic while generics keep it static and allocation-free; in an async UI runtime the wrapper must also forward the runtime's traits, not only the component trait. The hand-written wrapper stays the right choice whenever the enhancement must preserve the exact trait surface, and it is unavoidable for method interception, which the language does not offer.
pitfalls: A returned impl Fn closure captures its environment: the wrapped component must be moved in or shared via Rc/Arc, and the returned closure is only 'static when it borrows nothing local.
A wrapper that forwards only some trait methods silently drops the rest, including default methods callers rely on; with trait objects every expected method must be forwarded.
Deref-based delegation looks convenient but leaks the inner component's whole API and makes the wrapper's surface unpredictable; explicit trait forwarding is the honest form.
